name: Ironfall
description: Ironfall rotates through a graveyard of its own making, the intense magnetic anomalies at its poles having claimed countless satellites, probes, and unwary ships over the centuries. The wreckage forms a halo of debris in unstable orbits, metal rain that falls unpredictably to the surface below. The mountains that thrust up from impact-scarred plains are rich with metallic ores, their peaks sometimes sparking with induced electrical discharge as the magnetic field fluctuates.

The lack of atmosphere means the debris arrives at full velocity, hypersonic impacts that have sculpted the landscape into a chaos of overlapping craters. Walking the surface requires constant situational awareness, debris tracking, and a healthy acceptance of risk. The magnetic storms play havoc with electronics, requiring hardened equipment and redundant systems for any extended operation. Yet the same forces that make Ironfall dangerous also make it valuable.

The metal content of the surface exceeds any surveyed body in the sector, concentrated by billions of years of debris accumulation. Mining operations have established hardened facilities in magnetically stable zones, extracting premium ores between storm cycles. The work is dangerous and well-compensated, attracting crews willing to trade safety for credits. Casualty rates remain high but acceptable by frontier standards.

The satellite graveyard in orbit has become a salvage destination in its own right, derelict craft from dozens of civilizations tumbling through the debris field. Some predate human spaceflight by millennia, their technology incomprehensible, their purposes unknown. Recovery operations focus on human-era wrecks, but occasionally something older makes it to the surface—artifacts that fetch prices high enough to justify the magnetic gauntlet that guards them. Ironfall takes what it wants from those who approach. Sometimes, it gives something back.
